about: Website editorial titles and descriptions. Runtime application metadata remains in catalog/entries/.

case-zero.title: League tables and report cards
case-zero.description: Compare the directions stated by a strict ranking and by KRW’s report cards for 97 firms.

noisy-estimate.title: Estimates and sampling error
noisy-estimate.description: Repeated samples give different estimates of the same true value. The spread depends on the standard error.

noisy-league.title: Ranking noisy estimates
noisy-league.description: Units estimated with less precision can appear at the extremes of a league table more often.

winners-curse.title: Selection bias at the extremes of a ranking
winners-curse.description: Selecting the highest or lowest estimates can introduce bias. The choice of prior changes the bias after shrinkage.

shrinkage.title: Normal–normal posterior shrinkage
shrinkage.description: Larger standard errors give the prior mean more weight. The units can change order after shrinkage.

shrinkage-price.title: Sensitivity to the prior standard deviation
shrinkage-price.description: A change in the prior standard deviation affects squared error and the certainty of pairwise comparisons differently.

posterior-pipeline.title: From data to posterior decisions
posterior-pipeline.description: Follow two estimates through posterior shrinkage to a decision about whether to state their order.

two-units.title: Pairwise posterior direction probabilities
two-units.description: With two independent normal posteriors, the probability that A is higher depends on the mean and standard deviation of their difference.

correlated-units.title: Posterior dependence and pairwise comparisons
correlated-units.description: Changing posterior correlation can change the probability that one unit is higher even when both marginal distributions stay fixed.

beyond-normal.title: Marginal summaries and joint direction probabilities
beyond-normal.description: Two examples show how posterior shape and dependence can change direction probabilities at fixed marginal means.

interval-overlap.title: Marginal interval overlap and direction probabilities
interval-overlap.description: The probability that one unit is higher can be substantial even when their marginal credible intervals overlap.

overlap-in-the-league.title: Interval overlap across 435 pairs
overlap-in-the-league.description: Compare interval overlap and posterior direction probabilities for all 435 pairs in a simulated league.

pairwise-matrix.title: The matrix of pairwise posterior probabilities
pairwise-matrix.description: Reordering the units moves the cells of the matrix while preserving the probability attached to each pair.

which-ranking.title: Alternative rankings from a posterior distribution
which-ranking.description: Ranking units by posterior mean, expected rank, or probability of reaching a top group can produce different orders.

majority-wins.title: Majority comparisons and expected ranks
majority-wins.description: A count of pairwise majority wins records which direction is more likely. Expected rank also uses the size of each probability.

ranking-claims.title: Expected errors in a strict ranking
ranking-claims.description: Add the posterior error probabilities for all pairwise directions in a strict ranking to find its expected wrong count.

mc-error.title: Monte Carlo error in pairwise probabilities
mc-error.description: With a finite set of posterior draws, sampling error can change the report chosen near a decision boundary.

chain-draws.title: Monte Carlo error with dependent draws
chain-draws.description: Draws from a stationary two-state Markov chain show how dependence affects estimates of a direction probability.

one-pair.title: The decision for an isolated pair
one-pair.description: The cheapest action for a single pair depends on its posterior direction probabilities and the cost of withholding.

report-builder.title: Grade reports as pairwise decisions
report-builder.description: Assign units to ordered grades to see which pairwise directions the report states and which it leaves open.

how-many-reports.title: The number of ordered grade reports
how-many-reports.description: Count the possible reports and see how a grade cap or a fixed order reduces the number of candidates.

price-of-silence.title: Reporting risk and withholding cost
price-of-silence.description: Reporting risk adds expected wrong directions to the cost of leaving comparisons unstated.

tau-path.title: Optimal reports along the withholding-cost path
tau-path.description: A report’s risk is a line in the withholding cost. The optimal report changes where the lowest line switches.

coherence.title: Coherence constraints on pairwise decisions
coherence.description: Decisions made one pair at a time can conflict with the ordering required by a grade report.

coherence-finite.title: Coherence in a finite three-unit example
coherence-finite.description: Evaluate all 13 reports for three units under the same four-state posterior.

disclosed-errors.title: Expected and realized errors among stated directions
disclosed-errors.description: Compare the expected wrong share, the wrong count in a posterior state, and the probability that every stated direction is correct.

reported-and-realized.title: Reported error and reference-law evaluation
reported-and-realized.description: Compare what the posterior predicts about errors with the errors observed when the true values are held fixed.

frontier.title: The error–disclosure frontier
frontier.description: The lower convex boundary shows the smallest expected wrong count attainable at each mean number of stated pairs.

frontier-mixtures.title: Mixtures of frontier reports
frontier-mixtures.description: Choose between two complete reports at random to reach an intermediate expected number of stated pairs.

families.title: Restrictions on the report family
families.description: Grade caps, exact grade counts, and fixed orders restrict the search in different ways. The minimum risk depends on the family.

report-card.title: Posterior summaries in a grade report
report-card.description: The card shows each unit’s posterior interval and the expected error of comparisons between grades.

two-denominators.title: Error rates under two denominators
two-denominators.description: The same expected wrong count can be expressed per possible pair or per stated pair. The two rates answer different questions.

ties-and-withholding.title: Posterior equality and withholding
ties-and-withholding.description: Positive probability of equality changes the cost of making a strict statement. The preferred action depends on how equality is scored.

computing-grades.title: Computation of optimal grade reports
computing-grades.description: Enumeration, cuts of a fixed order, and a joint search give different kinds of answers about which report is best.

another-law.title: Evaluation under an alternative posterior law
another-law.description: Evaluate the same report under two posterior laws to see how its risk and regret change.

chosen-and-judged.title: Selection and evaluation using posterior draws
chosen-and-judged.description: A report can look better on the draws that selected it than when evaluated under the exact posterior law.

averaging-errors.title: Averaging error shares across reports
averaging-errors.description: When reports state different numbers of pairs, pooling their errors and averaging their error shares can give different answers.

one-correction.title: Sensitivity to corrections and unit removal
one-correction.description: Compare which pairwise statements change after revising one unit’s marginal distribution or removing a unit.

fixed-tiers.title: Fixed quantile tiers
fixed-tiers.description: Group the estimates by quantiles, then use the posterior to count the expected mistakes in the resulting report.

tier-sizes.title: Disclosure determined by tier sizes
tier-sizes.description: The number of stated pairs depends on the sizes of the tiers. Compare counts across all ordered size choices.

evidence-flags.title: Grades based on standardized evidence
evidence-flags.description: Turn estimates and standard errors into evidence flags, then examine the pairwise directions the flags imply.

flags-in-the-league.title: Standardized-evidence flags in a league
flags-in-the-league.description: Evaluate the directions and posterior risk of a flag report for a simulated league of thirty units.

posterior-tiers.title: Tiers and optimized cuts of posterior rankings
posterior-tiers.description: Compare fixed tiers, boundaries chosen along a posterior order, and a search over reports that can change that order.

order-misses.title: Restrictions imposed by a fixed order
order-misses.description: At some withholding costs in this example, cuts of the posterior-mean order miss the best unrestricted report.

rule-comparison.title: Comparison at matched disclosure
rule-comparison.description: For each rule, compare its expected wrong count with the frontier at the same number of stated pairs.

same-tau-or-same-n.title: Common withholding cost and matched disclosure
same-tau-or-same-n.description: A common withholding cost compares risk. A common number of stated pairs compares expected errors at the same disclosure.

deciles-quartiles.title: Deciles and quartiles of posterior means
deciles-quartiles.description: Compare deciles and quartiles of posterior means on KRW’s measures of discordance and informativeness.

naive-thresholding.title: Coherence of pairwise threshold decisions
naive-thresholding.description: Pairwise thresholds can produce incompatible triples. KRW’s archived cards show which directions a coherent report states.

better-on-average.title: Expected and state-specific reporting loss
better-on-average.description: A report with smaller posterior expected loss can still have larger loss in an individual posterior draw.

stability.title: Report stability under repeated measurement
stability.description: Repeat measurement at fixed true values to see which directions are newly stated, withheld, or reversed.

one-place.title: Reporting, allocation and classification
one-place.description: Reporting a direction, allocating a place, and classifying a unit at a threshold use different decision rules.

several-criteria.title: Posterior profiles on multiple criteria
several-criteria.description: Compare the same units on two scores. Their posterior order and direction probabilities can differ by score.

conflict-pairs.title: Opposing criterion directions
conflict-pairs.description: When two criteria favor different directions, compare the posterior evidence and the costs of stating either one.

two-scores.title: A common grade report for two scores
two-scores.description: Use one grade column for both scores and see how its expected errors are distributed across the criteria.

weight-path.title: Optimal reports along the criterion-weight path
weight-path.description: As the criterion weights change, a different report can minimize risk. The graph marks the weight ranges for each report.

common-grade-cost.title: Criterion-specific excess risk of a common report
common-grade-cost.description: Compare each criterion’s risk under the common grades with its minimum risk in the same report family.

composite-or-criterion.title: Composite targets and criterion directions
composite-or-criterion.description: A statement about a weighted composite and a statement about the component criteria can favor different reports.

error-budgets.title: Criterion-specific expected-error budgets
error-budgets.description: An error limit on each criterion restricts which grade reports can be selected.

criterion-mixture.title: A random-criterion representation of weighted risk
criterion-mixture.description: For a fixed report, weighting criterion risks gives the same expected risk as randomly drawing a criterion with those weights.

worst-criterion.title: Minimizing the largest criterion risk
worst-criterion.description: Compare the report that minimizes weighted risk with the report that minimizes the largest criterion risk.

choosing-settings.title: Sensitivity to costs, weights and grade restrictions
choosing-settings.description: Change withholding costs, weights, and grade restrictions separately to see why the chosen report changes.

draws-to-errors.title: Pairwise errors from joint posterior draws
draws-to-errors.description: Pairwise errors depend on which unit values occur together in the same posterior draw.

why-withheld.title: Reasons for a withheld comparison
why-withheld.description: A pair can share a grade because of its own error probabilities, a conflict between criteria, or restrictions on the full report.

pairs-leave-open.title: Quantities not identified by pairwise probabilities
pairs-leave-open.description: The same pairwise probabilities can accompany different probabilities for a composite direction or for all statements being correct.

estimated-budgets.title: Error budgets under estimated pairwise probabilities
estimated-budgets.description: When a proposed bound on Monte Carlo error holds, it identifies reports that meet an error budget under the exact probabilities.

lambda-tau.title: KRW's reward and postrank's withholding cost
lambda-tau.description: Convert KRW’s reward to postrank’s withholding cost under the assumptions that make the two losses comparable.

krw-axes.title: Equivalent reporting-loss scales
krw-axes.description: The two losses order the six-site reports in the same way under the stated assumptions.

krw-card.title: KRW's race and gender report cards
krw-card.description: Read the posterior intervals and directions in KRW’s published race and gender report cards for 97 firms.

krw-heatmap.title: Firm-pair probabilities and report-card blocks
krw-heatmap.description: Compare pairwise thresholds with the directions actually stated by KRW’s archived grade reports.

krw-lambda.title: KRW's archived reward path
krw-lambda.description: As the reward for correct directions changes, KRW’s archived cards state different numbers of pairs and incur different expected errors.

signed-or-absolute.title: Signed and absolute gender-gap targets
signed-or-absolute.description: A signed gap and its absolute size are different targets. Their pairwise probabilities and fixed-order reports can differ.

krw-two.title: A common report for race and gender gaps
krw-two.description: Compare a common grade report with KRW’s separate race and gender cards using the same weighted expected loss.

cde-cuts.title: School tertiles and minimum-risk grades
cde-cuts.description: For twelve schools, compare chronic absence tertiles with the grades that minimize risk under the same posterior.

cde-one-disclosure.title: School reports at matched disclosure
cde-one-disclosure.description: Compare expected wrong counts across three-grade reports that all state 48 school pairs.

cde-pair.title: A high-probability school comparison withheld
cde-pair.description: See how requiring the report to put school F above school I changes the best report in the same family.

cde-tau-path.title: School-report changes along the withholding-cost path
cde-tau-path.description: As the cost of withholding rises, the optimal report changes how many school pairs it states and which ones it states.

alabama-map.title: A common report for Alabama county outcomes
alabama-map.description: Compare the same county grades on historical income and incarceration outcomes.

your-data.title: Reports from supplied posterior summaries
your-data.description: Enter normal summaries, estimates with a prior, or pairwise probabilities to calculate a grade report in the browser.

report-designer.title: Case-report specification and export
report-designer.description: Choose settings for a released case, check expected errors by criterion, and export the report and its inputs.

profile-common-vs-domain.title: Common or profile?
profile-common-vs-domain.description: Compare one shared grade column with two domain columns under the same posterior and loss.

profile-separability.title: Separate or joint?
profile-separability.description: Separate domain choices can minimize additive loss. A joint error limit can make their combination infeasible.

profile-dependence.title: Error overlap
profile-dependence.description: The same domain posteriors can lead to different best profiles when their errors overlap differently.

profile-resolution.title: Budget and grades
profile-resolution.description: A looser error limit can increase reporting detail in one domain and reduce it in another.

fictional-site-profiles.title: Site profiles
fictional-site-profiles.description: Read two grades for each of forty fictional sites and compare the directions stated within each domain.
